cur:catacombs2-balazuc-sarcophagus.summary: Seven niches crowned by alternating pediments and arches, separated by spiral columns, frame biblical scenes on this Arles-made sarcophagus found in the Ardèche. Christ raises Lazarus, heals the paralytic and a blind man and foretells Peter's denial, while at one end Job sits in conversation with his friends. The photograph shows it in 2022, when it was lent to the Lyon Biennale of contemporary art.
facts: It was discovered in the 16th century at Les Salles, in the commune of Balazuc (Ardèche), and long kept in the church of Saint-Maurice-d'Ardèche.
In 1851 it went to the Musée des Beaux-Arts in Lyon and later to the Gallo-Roman museum at Fourvière (now Lugdunum); a cast is shown in Balazuc town hall.
The scenes were identified by the abbé Joseph-Alexandre Martigny in a memoir published in 1864.

cur:objects-lyon-christ-pantocrator-ivor.summary: A half-length Christ fills this ivory plaque, his bearded face framed by long hair and a cross-nimbus, the abbreviation of his name carved on either side. He raises his right hand in blessing and holds against his chest a gospel book with a jewelled cover. The intense, frontal gaze is the image of the Pantocrator, the Ruler of All, that Byzantine artists placed in domes, on coins and on precious objects alike.
facts: The museum label identifies it as a Byzantine work of the late 10th or early 11th century, 12.9 cm high, inventory L 412.
The bust of Christ holding a book and blessing became, after the end of Iconoclasm in 843, the standard Byzantine image of Christ Pantocrator (type).

feat:stuma-paten-communion-of-the-apostl.summary: On this silver liturgical plate, Christ appears twice behind an altar: on one side he gives the consecrated bread, on the other the cup, to apostles who come forward with reverently bowed heads. The scene shows the Last Supper not as a historical meal but as the heavenly liturgy, with Christ himself as the celebrant of every Eucharist. The paten would have held the bread during the Divine Liturgy, so that the image and the sacrament met on the same surface.
facts: Official control stamps on the back date the silver to the reign of Emperor Justin II (565–578).
It was found in the early twentieth century at Stuma in northern Syria, and scholars have associated it with the group of village church silver known as the Kaper Koraon Treasure.
A near-twin, the Riha Paten, is at Dumbarton Oaks in Washington, D.C.; both were gifts of donors to Syrian village churches.
The 'Communion of the Apostles' became a standard subject for the apses of Byzantine churches, directly above the altar.

Q60794462.summary: Behind the high altar of the new Coventry Cathedral, built beside the ruins of the medieval cathedral destroyed by bombing in 1940, Christ sits enthroned in a vast green field. He is enclosed in a mandorla and surrounded by the four living creatures of the Apocalypse that stand for the Evangelists. Below him, Sutherland placed a small Crucifixion, joining the Christ of the Passion to the Christ of glory in a single image of hope after war.
facts: At about 23 by 12 metres, it was one of the largest tapestries in the world when it was made.
A life-size human figure stands between Christ's feet, showing how huge the enthroned Christ is.
It was woven in a single piece by the Pinton workshop in Felletin, near Aubusson, and was installed for the cathedral's consecration in May 1962.
